description: Proposes next week's strength sessions from the stored plan (set_plan), what the user's journal says they ACTUALLY lifted (log_session), and how recovered and loaded they are. It writes NOTHING: it returns a proposal that the caller shows to the user and may pass on, there is no auto-write (reading the history fills only the same rebuildable derived-data cache as get_exercise_history; nothing is sent to the watch). To put the proposal in the approval queue, pass its `queuePayload` (exactly queue_adjustment's arguments) to queue_adjustment: nothing is queued by this tool, and nothing is pushed until the user approves with resolve_approval. With `predict: true` it also returns, for each proposed INCREASE, a ready log_prediction payload in `predictions` (kind reps_hit, date = the session's date, rule 'progression'; probability = the user's own hit rate for that rule from get_prediction_stats once 20 are scored, else 0.65, always kept inside 0.5 to 0.9); it never logs them itself. The base week is the latest week of the plan (within 4 weeks before weekStart) with a guided session; its sessions are repeated one week on (weekStart = a Monday after today, default the next Monday) with each exercise's load decided by a small closed set of NAMED rules, reported in `rulesUsed` with their values (`rules` overrides some, each inside a stated range; unknown names are refused). PROGRESS: in the lift's latest logged session every planned set reached its planned reps at one weight -> load + one step (get_exercise_history's suggestion: at most incrementKg, default 2.5 kg, at most 5% of the load, at least 1.25 kg). HOLD: anything else with evidence -> the load that was done is repeated. DELOAD (load lowered deloadPct, default 10%, rounded to 1.25 kg): stallSessions (default 2) logged sessions of the lift in a row without hitting the plan; OR today's TSB (get_training_load) below tsbDeloadBelow (default -25); OR HRV and recovery on waking (get_baselines, today) both below the user's band. NEVER raises a load without evidence: a lift with no log_session entry for the plan's own sets x reps is left as it is (and the watch records only the plan, not what was lifted), one of HRV / recovery below the band or an unread part of the history blocks every increase, and a lift whose detail has no kg ('BW 3x15', 'RPE6') or no 'NxM' is never touched. The result is `insufficient` (status, `missing` says what; sessions, guides and forecast empty or null: no changes proposed) when there is no plan, no guided session to repeat, fewer than 2 sessions with logged sets in the last 8 weeks, or no lift with usable evidence. Output: { status ('ok' | 'insufficient'), weekStart, weekEnd, asOf (today), planSource ('stored' | 'demo' | 'none'), rulesUsed: [{ name, value, default, overridden, overridable, rule }], missing, basedOn: { from, to }, signals: { ctl, atl, tsb, hrv, recoveryMorning (below | within | above | null) }, sessions: [{ date, title, guide? }] (pass to set_plan; mode 'merge' replaces the plan's sessions on those dates), guides: [strength guide specs] (pass to push_week_plan, dryRun by default; each exercise's `last` and `target` are set for the watch), changes: [{ date, session, exercise, action ('progress' | 'hold' | 'deload' | 'unchanged'), changed, from: { detail, kg }, to: { detail, kg }, reasons }] (every exercise, with the reasons for it), reasons (what applies to the whole week), forecast: { asOf, start, series: [{ date, tss, ctl, atl, tsb }], basis } (forecast_training_load's own projection from today's values through the proposed week), risk: { level ('none' | 'caution'), flags: [{ rule, detail }], tsbFloor: { threshold (default -30), minTsb, date }, weeklyLoad: { threshold (default 30 %), proposedTss, previous4wAvgTss, jumpPct, complete } } (flags: the forecast TSB below tsbRiskFloor, or the week's TSS more than weeklyJumpPct over the average week of the 28 days before it, the upper edge of the 0.8-1.3 acute:chronic range: heuristics, not safe/unsafe lines), queuePayload ({ kind: 'week_plan', payload: { guides }, forDate (the earliest guide's date), reasons, source } to pass to queue_adjustment as it is; null when nothing is proposed), predictions: [{ session, payload (log_prediction's arguments), basis: { source ('history' | 'default'), rule, n, hitRate } }] (empty unless predict), estimates: [{ date, title, tss, sessions, scope }] (each session's TSS for the forecast: the median of the user's last 90 days' sessions of the same title, at least 2 needed, else null and counted as 0), history: { from, to, guidedSessions, loggedSessions, pending, errors }, notes, errors }. MODEL-BASED: every number is a projection or a rule's output from the user's own data, not a measurement or a prediction of how they will respond; CTL can be about 1 point off the watch. Read-only.

predict.description: true: also return a ready log_prediction payload per proposed increase in `predictions` (never logged by this tool). Default false.

rules.description: Optional overrides of the named rules (unknown names are refused). Each is a number inside the stated range; leave out what should stay at its default.

deloadPct.description: A deload lowers the load by this percent, rounded to 1.25 kg.

incrementKg.description: Largest load step of a progression, in kg (never more than 5% of the load, never less than 1.25 kg).

stallSessions.description: Logged sessions of one lift in a row that did not hit every planned set and rep at one weight; reaching this many deloads the lift.

tsbDeloadBelow.description: Every load with a kg figure is deloaded when today's TSB (Form) is below this.

tsbRiskFloor.description: The forecast flags the week when its lowest TSB is below this (-30 is the 'high risk' zone of the usual Form scale).

weeklyJumpPct.description: The forecast flags the week when its TSS is more than this percent above the average week of the 28 days before it (acute:chronic about 1.3).

weekStart.description: The Monday the proposed week starts on, YYYY-MM-DD; must be after today. Default: the next Monday.

name: propose_next_week
title: Propose next week's strength sessions (read-only: returns a proposal and a queuePayload, writes nothing)
